title: The real story behind brand growth, told over dinner | OFF THE RECORD
summary: On the last day of September, K-beauty and fashion leaders met at MarqVision's first OFF THE RECORD to trade lessons on global expansion, distribution and brand protection.
body_markdown:
##### **Key takeaways**


- Sustained global growth takes more than new markets. Brands also have to manage distribution and customer trust.
- At the first OFF THE RECORD, K-beauty and fashion leaders shared the choices and missteps behind their growth, and made new connections.


## **The last day of September, and the story behind growth**


On September 30, 2026, MarqVision hosted the first OFF THE RECORD: Behind K-Beauty & Fashion with brand leaders driving K-beauty and fashion.


The invitation-only networking dinner focused on how growth happens, not on the results. Which decisions sparked growth? What turned out differently than expected? What needs to be ready for the next market? Leaders facing similar questions looked to each other’s experience for clues to their next move.


## **What brands need to watch as they grow**


More countries and sales channels mean more opportunity, but also more ground a brand can’t check on directly. Unfamiliar sellers, unstable prices, content used without permission, and customers asking whether a product is genuine all land in different departments. In the end, they all affect revenue, distribution and customer trust.


In the opening session, MarqVision laid out a direction for running a brand: connect these market signals through data, then use AI to turn them into decisions and action. The message was to treat brand protection not as a response after something goes wrong, but as a management discipline for preparing and sustaining growth.


## **Beyond takedown counts: a standard for protecting the next stage of growth**


The brand leader panel made the case for looking at customer experience, distribution and rights protection together. A question about product quality can be a signal to check distribution channels. An individual online sales problem may be tied to a larger supply chain.


When entering a new market, it pays to prepare in advance: secure your rights, set up distribution contracts, manage evidence and decide who responds. It’s not only about how many listings you found and removed. It’s also whether customers can buy with confidence, and whether official distributors and partners can keep their business running smoothly.


The question the conversation left behind was clear. Beyond solving today’s problems, is your brand ready to protect its next stage of growth?


## **A conversation that started on stage and continued at the table**


After the panel, guests moved between two color-coded zones, “Global market expansion” and “E-commerce and distribution strategy,” for dinner and networking. With leaders who shared the same interests seated together, the conversation got more specific: how to choose a new market, how to manage pricing and sales channels, how to work with partners.


What helped growth, and where did unexpected trouble come up? As leaders talked openly about the concerns and missteps behind their growth, one brand’s experience became a useful perspective for another brand’s next decision. Conversations that started that evening carried on after the event.


The post-event survey confirmed the value of these exchanges. Every response to whether the networking was helpful was positive, and every overall satisfaction rating was 4 or higher out of 5.


## **OFF THE RECORD continues**


The first gathering showed that when leaders with similar challenges simply share their experience, new perspectives and connections follow.


OFF THE RECORD will continue the conversation with focused topics for specific industries, roles and stages of growth. We’ll meet again to talk about the choices, missteps and next challenges that results alone don’t reveal.


What story will the next OFF THE RECORD start?


## **FAQ: common questions**


**Q. Who is it for?**


It’s an invitation-only networking event for decision-makers and hands-on leaders at K-beauty and fashion brands working on global expansion and brand operations. Attendees look at real-world challenges such as distribution, customer trust and brand protection through each other’s experience.


**Q. How is it different from a typical seminar?**


It doesn’t end with listening to presentations. Over dinner and open networking, attendees share their own experience with each other. At the first gathering, we ran two color-coded zones, “Global market expansion” and “E-commerce and distribution strategy,” and MarqVision hosts introduced leaders with similar interests.


**Q. What was the key message of this event?**


Treat brand protection not as cleanup after growth, but as part of the operations that prepare for the next stage of growth. We shared a way of connecting unusual market signals to distribution and customer experience, and of looking beyond takedown counts to customer trust and the stability of official channels.


**Q. When is the next event?**


We’ll announce the date and topic on MarqVision’s official channels once they’re confirmed.
